title: Open-loop and closed-loop control compared
examples: What is the difference between open-loop and closed-loop control?
Is a timer open loop or closed loop?

explain.say: Every automatic machine follows a control system. In open-loop control it does what it was told without checking; in closed-loop control it measures the result and corrects itself.

explain.say: A garden sprinkler on a timer is open loop: it waters for twenty minutes even if it is pouring with rain. It is simple and cheap, but it cannot notice when something changes.

faq.q: What is a closed-loop control system?
faq.a: It is a system that measures its own output and uses that measurement to correct itself. A sensor feeds back what is happening so the controller can shrink the error between actual and target.

faq.q: What is an open-loop control system?
faq.a: It carries out a set action without measuring the result, like traffic lights on a fixed timer or a sprinkler that runs for set minutes. It cannot correct for surprises.

faq.q: What is the error in a control system?
faq.a: The error is the difference between where you want to be, the set point, and where you actually are. A closed-loop controller acts to shrink the error towards zero.
asks: What does error mean in control?

faq.a: Not always. Open loop is simpler, cheaper and fine when conditions barely change. Closed loop needs sensors and costs more, and badly tuned feedback can wobble or overshoot.
The set point is the target value a controller is trying to reach, like 100 kilometres per hour on cruise control or 21 degrees on a heating system.
asks: What is a target value in control?

facts: James Watt's centrifugal governor of 1788 was an early feedback controller that kept a steam engine's speed steady.
Your body uses feedback control to keep its temperature near 37 degrees Celsius.

quiz.say: A sprinkler waters for 20 minutes every evening, even when it rains. What kind of control is this?
quiz.show: A timed sprinkler that ignores rain is…
quiz.why: It follows a fixed plan and never measures the result, which is open-loop control.

wrong.1: A closed loop would check the soil or rain and adjust.
wrong.2: Feedback means measuring the result, which this sprinkler never does.
